Genesis 1:2 • Hebrew Word Study

The Deep

תְּהוֹם
Tehom
the deep • the depths • deep waters
“And the earth was formless and void, and darkness was over the face of the deep.”
← Back to Bible Study

Follow the Word

GENESIS 1:2
The deep at the beginning.

GENESIS 7:11
The fountains of the great deep.

PSALM 106:9
God leads His people through the depths.

HABAKKUK 3:15
God walks through the great waters.

Faith & Application

What looks unsurvivably deep to us is not beyond God.

One of the first Hebrew words that stopped me in my tracks was tehom—“the deep.”

What is “the deep”?

I know when something is over my head, it’s deep. Surely “the deep” of the Bible is deeper than 5’1”… But what is the deep?

The Bible describes it like a place, and from what I understand, it is the watery depths. I’m still not sure why I got hung up on it, but here we are.

Genesis 7:11 uses tehom when it says, “All the fountains of the great deep were broken up, and the windows of heaven were opened.”

This was the beginning of the torrential downpour of the great flood back in Noah’s day. We all know how deep that got… death and destruction everywhere.

Psalm 106:9: “He rebuked the Red Sea also, and it was dried up: so he led them through the depths.”

What would have been their deaths, being lost in the depths, God dried up and walked them through it.

Never discount the power of God and how He can transform an impossible, unsurvivable, hopelessly deep, insurmountable problem.

Because just when you think there’s no way out, and darkness is over the face of the deep, God can speak light, and there will be light. And He will say, “It’s all good.”

Is this an oversimplification of a problem? Does this feel like a minimization?

No.

The power of God has no good description. And until we let the breath of God breathe on our situation and believe that He’s in complete control, we’ll be treading water up to our noses over and over.

God says in His Word that He is greater than anything else here.

And can you imagine facing the depths of the Red Sea, and suddenly it’s all gone, dried up?

God then walks you through the depths like they are nothing at all.

HABAKKUK 3:15
“Thou didst walk through the sea with thine horses, through the heap of great waters.”

Habakkuk gives us another striking picture: God Himself moving through the great waters—the tehom.

Now that’s deep.
